# Genuine source projective normalizers do not preserve maximum-field capacity

The new weighted surface theorem handles one compatible weight of the form
`g H/L^d`, with a common affine positive denominator. The following exact
example shows that the ACTUAL maximum of two source-normalized projective
fields need not have this property. The continuous normalizers are nonzero;
the simplest version uses zero base shifts. Even varying every positive
affine base extension does not repair the ceiling-one obstruction while
the same flat contact support planes are retained.

This is a capacity obstruction, not an OC counterexample or a certificate
that a critical cap system cannot choose other sources/support slopes.

## 1. Actual body, source points, and optimal projective parameters

Take n=1,d=2 and

    C=[-1,1]_z x [-1,1]_x x [-1,1]_y.

Its integer fibers are the three identical squares K=[-1,1]^2. On the
common top facet y=1 use tangential coordinate x and outward normal
u=(0,1). Choose sources at the endpoint bases,

    (z_-,Y_-)=(-1,(-8/13,0)),
    (z_+,Y_+)=( 1,( 8/13,0)).

Both continuous points are interior to their actual squares. Their
optimal source-centered projective denominators are

    L_-^own(x,y)=(13/9)(1+x/2),
    L_+^own(x,y)=(13/9)(1-x/2).                       (1)

To check optimality directly, for L=1+x/2 compute

    integral_(-1)^1 L^-4 dx =416/81,
    integral_(-1)^1 x L^-4 dx =-256/81.

The escort mean is -8/13, and the y escort mean vanishes by symmetry.
Also L_-^own=1+(13/18)(x+8/13), so the derivative of the projective-volume
objective with respect to its two parameters is zero at (13/18,0).
The objective is strictly convex on its positive-denominator domain,
hence this is its unique minimizer. Reflection proves the plus case.
Thus (1) is not an arbitrary inverse-power weight chosen after the fact.

The source support heights on the top facet are both one. Put

    kappa=(9/13)^2=81/169.

Their source boundary potentials there are exactly

    Phi_-(x)=kappa/(1+x/2)^2,
    Phi_+(x)=kappa/(1-x/2)^2.                         (2)

For the actual global supporting-cut construction choose the feasible
flat support slopes A_-=A_+=0. These expose all three top facets. With
zero base shifts the first boundary speed from applying both source
cuts is the physical maximum

    W_z(x)=max(Phi_-(x),Phi_+(x))
          =kappa/(1-|x|/2)^2                        (3)

on every top facet, including the middle one.

## 2. A same-parity midpoint coupling exceeds the actual target capacity

At base -1 take gamma_- to be the measure on the top-facet interval
x in [-1,-3/4] with density Phi_-. At base 1 take gamma_+ on
x in [3/4,1] with density Phi_+. Both are dominated by their actual
maximum-field capacities (3). Their common mass is

    m=kappa integral_(-1)^(-3/4) (1+x/2)^-2 dx
     =4kappa/5.                                     (4)

The endpoint bases have the same original integer parity. Every coupling
of these two marginals has midpoint base zero and tangential midpoint
in I=[-1/8,1/8]. An old integer-midpoint coupling exists explicitly:
reflect x to -x, which sends every midpoint to x=0.

The full available maximum-field capacity on the forced midpoint interval
is only

    integral_I W_0(x)dx
      =2kappa integral_0^(1/8) (1-x/2)^-2 dx
      =4kappa/15.                                   (5)

Thus no coupling with these marginals can have midpoint density at most
W_0. Even a density ceiling 2W_0 is insufficient. Every feasible ceiling
factor is at least m/(4kappa/15)=3, exceeding the n=1 parity factor 2.
This obstruction precedes and therefore also defeats any additional
convex-order domination requirement on the old midpoint law.

## 3. No positive affine base extension restores ceiling one

Retain the two source charts (1) and the flat support slopes, but allow
arbitrary affine base extensions. After factoring out 13/9 write them as

    ell_-(z,x)=1+x/2+b_-(z+1),
    ell_+(z,x)=1-x/2+b_+(z-1).

Suppose both are strictly positive on the entire actual body C. Evaluate
the first at z=1,x=-1 and the second at z=-1,x=1. Necessarily

    b_->-1/4,       b_+<1/4.

Consequently at base zero,

    ell_-(0,x)>3/4+x/2,
    ell_+(0,x)>3/4-x/2.

The actual middle maximum is therefore bounded above by
kappa/(3/4-|x|/2)^2. Its capacity on the same forced midpoint interval
satisfies

    integral_I W_0 dx
      <4kappa[1/(3/4-1/16)-1/(3/4)]
      =16kappa/33 < 4kappa/5=m.                     (6)

The input measures (4) remain unchanged, because a base extension is zero
at its own source base; they remain dominated by the endpoint maximum
fields. Thus no globally positive affine base extension repairs the
ceiling-one midpoint property at this fixed common support contact.
The density factor required by (6) is at least 33/20.

A stronger numerical consequence holds for extensions retaining the
canonical normalization floor L_normalized>=1/(d+1)=1/3 throughout C.
Then ell>=3/13, so b_->=-7/52 and b_+<=7/52. The middle capacity on I
is at most

    4kappa[1/(45/52-1/16)-1/(45/52)]
      =(2704/7515)kappa.

The required factor is at least 1503/676>2. Thus within this common
canonical floor class, even the full 2^n factor does not repair the
maximum-field capacity.

## 4. What survives and what remains a distinct obligation

Each individual field in (2) is a legitimate projective boundary
potential and belongs to the new weighted transport class. The actual
joint speed is a maximum of DIFFERENT denominators, which need not belong
to that class. Replacing it by a common field or summing independently
repaired source transports requires a separate capacity argument.

This example fixes flat support slopes so that the same normal contacts
all three fibers. Endpoint source bases permit other supporting slopes
that isolate their fibers; the example does not assert that every global
cut choice fails. It also does not assert these two sources or their
selected face marginals arise from an optimal critical cap law. Those
additional structures could still provide a new selection or payment
mechanism. The exact conclusion is that the proved weighted transport
closure alone does not supply the maximum-field step used by simultaneous
projective erosions, even for genuine source-normalized charts.
